scientific_question: Can 4-weight learned contextual identity-link similarity trained on deliberately deceptive near-negative pairs outperform strong pre-registered Euclidean cutoff heuristics while enabling native recurrent multi-path reasoning?

design.training_examples: 256 same-identity pairs, 256 distinct-identity near-impostors with +0.045 displacement of first contextual node coordinate
design.model: logistic squared fingerprint distances scaled 1000, frozen after 700 training epochs, fixed .012 gradient step
design.source_generator: hard near-matches created for unrelated decoy IDs, aliases share latent profile; other source graph construction inherited unchanged from F24

controls: new trained hard-negative logistic identity similarity
